legend: An osteochondroma of the right distal femur in a 17-year-old boy. Lateral radiograph showing a pedunculated osteochondroma arising from the posterior aspect of the bone. The cortex and medulla of the lesion are continuous with those of the femur.

Fat-saturated proton density (PD)-weighted axial MRI through the superior aspect of the osteochondroma. The lesion contains fatty marrow (asterisk) with some oedema-like signal medially. A layer of hyperintensity is seen on the surface (arrows), consistent with a thin cartilage cap.
Classic bosselated, smooth appearance of the external surface. The tumour is covered by a translucent fibrous layer (perichondrium).
Cross-section through a pedunculated osteochondroma, disclosing the typical hyaline cartilaginous cap. Note the continuation with the medullary canal showing fatty marrow.

Hyaline cartilaginous cap composed of bland chondrocytes located in large empty lacunae, piling up at the base of the cap. Note the bone encasement at the base and the progressive chondrocyte maturation from the base to the top, with corresponding change of the matrix quality.
Detail of the cap base. The chondrocytes have pinpoint nuclei and angulated cytoplasm hosted within large lacunae. Note the typical basophilia of the hyaline matrix.

Frontal radiograph of the right knee. There is a pedunculated osteochondroma arising from the metadiaphyseal junction and projecting away from the epiphysis of the medial cortex of the left distal femur.
